structural_exploration.basis: candidate selection for investigation; no cycle or speedup claim
structural_exploration.action: Continue optimization while timing coverage is repaired. Use legal pass/schedule alternatives and inspect their emitted products: operand traffic and reloads, packing frequency, storage lifetimes, tile coverage, completion boundaries and CPU work. Retain alternatives with different resource tradeoffs; check affected Spike numerics and independent shapes/tails. See cycle-model-and-gsim. Each passing case's calibrated fast estimate (evidence kind fast_estimate) ranks it until a complete estimate arrives: decide on it and revert if a later measurement disagrees. Large cases do not acquire gSIM permission.

unknown_timing.meaning: UNKNOWN timing is missing evidence, not a measured loss or a refusal of the variant. A variant whose timing is UNKNOWN is still a candidate; decide on its calibrated fast estimate (performance.fast_estimate, with its error band) and revert if a complete estimate or measurement later disagrees.
unknown_timing.how_to_measure: Performance is compared on the Spike cycle model by default (self-checks, --sweep, --panel, variants). Where the model reports UNKNOWN, request gSIM cycles for one named case per request: `python agent_selfcheck.py --capsules NAME --sim gsim --wait-budget 5`, then collect it with `--attach ID`. This admits required correctness cases under their own gSIM budget. To compare a variant, obtain a supported complete-scope observation of the primary workload. Control measurements serve correctness/calibration diagnostics, not routine performance tuning or a substitute performance result for a larger workload.
